question: Can full pairwise uniform disagreement rates on names of a first reached stage hide different next complete-step birth counts? Compare NAE and parity.
primary_observable: Exact canonical labelled and name-free rate relations, multiplicities of state sets and next birth counts across every actual first cut, and funded denominators in three independently seeded panels.
forbidden_inputs: Using a sorted list of rates as exact isomorphism, decorating rates by old/fresh names or source width, conflating no first cut with a reached zero count, using observed draws as all legitimate alternatives.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Literal parity and NAE pair rates and real ordinary births; closed eight-name supplied NAE alternatives versus actually reached stages; internal table automorphisms.
first_executable_signal: Complete enumeration of first reached stages from every eligible source of at most eight distinctions, grouped by the exact rate reading.
resource_budget: 6 GiB per process, initial 3–8 distinctions, 128 fresh draws per law and weighting, exact widths and controls; register any check expected to take over ten minutes.
stop_rule: Actual live NAE different-birth witness or exhaustive eight-distinction initial census and a named all-size class; finish conditional parity and fresh weighted comparisons.
decision_or_followup_rule: Report exact populations, model versus supplied choices, boundary of A97, and independent referee pending.
